thread:
mira: quick question — the SLO heatmap started showing repeated burn spikes in us-west-2 around 22:00 UTC yesterday that line up with node cordons. are we double-counting saturation SLI during drain windows? cc @carl @ada

carl: short answer: yes-ish. we currently compute saturation SLI from two sources: node-level GPU saturation and request queueing latency. when a node is cordoned we see both the node metric spike (pods reshuffled) and a transient latency bump while pod traffic moves. both contribute to the burn.

ada: i ran the prom query that backs the heatmap: 

```
# fraction of shards marked saturated over 5m
sum(gpu_saturated{region="us-west-2"}) / sum(gpu_total{region="us-west-2"})
```

that doesn't exclude maintenance windows or cordon labels. so the heatmap will show burn even if it's an operator-driven drain.

nina: is the cordon annotated anywhere? our maintenance pipeline should emit an annotation or a label on nodes, but we don't currently join that to the SLI timeseries.

mira: we do add a k8s annotation on nodes (`redwood/maintenance=true`) during planned drains but the metric exporter doesn't propagate that label to gpu_saturated.

josiah: options: (1) suppress alerts for known maintenance windows via Alertmanager mute_time_intervals/silences, (2) add a maintenance label to the recording rule so burn calc can exclude those times, or (3) discount maintenance from error budget accounting post-facto during the EB report.

carl: i prefer (2) because silences hide signals in the dashboards and (3) is retroactive which complicates automated rollouts. adding a maintenance label lets dashboards show a different burn category (maintenance vs real).

ada: agreed. proposal: create a recording rule that sets maintenance=1 for the duration of the cordon based on node annotations. pseudo-promql: 

```
record: maintenance_window{region="us-west-2"}
expr: max by(node) (kube_node_labels{label_redwood_maintenance="true"})
```

then change our burn rate calc to subtract maintenance-bound requests: 

```
errors = sum(increase(slo_errors_total{job="inference",region="us-west-2"}[1h]) unless on(node) maintenance_window == 1)
requests = sum(increase(slo_requests_total{job="inference",region="us-west-2"}[1h]) unless on(node) maintenance_window == 1)
burn = errors / requests
```

nina: small nit: promql `unless` semantics can be subtle if labels don't align; we may need to propagate the maintenance label onto request/error series at scrape time or use a join on `instance`/`node`.

josiah: if we can't reliably join, fallback is to emit a derived metric from the maintenance workflow itself: post a prometheus pushgateway or remote_write event that marks `maintenance_override{node=...,region=...}=1` when we start a cordon. then recordings are straightforward.

mira: what's the impact on error budget policy? do we exclude maintenance from the official burn (i.e., treat as exempt) or just show it separately? customers will ask if we're "gaming" our SLOs.

carl: recommend showing both: keep raw burn (what users saw) in reports for transparency, and compute an "adjusted burn" that excludes maintenance for operational escalation. E.g., dashboard panels: Raw burn, Maintenance burn, Adjusted burn. The EB alerting still uses adjusted burn for paging thresholds, but the monthly report highlights raw.

ada: implementation plan: 1) infra to emit maintenance_override metric (josiah), 2) recording rule to tag series (carl), 3) burn calc change + new grafana panels (nina), 4) update EB alerting to reference adjusted burn (mira).

josiah: i'll add a small webhook in the maintenance playbook that POSTs to pushgateway on start/stop. will put a TTL so missed stops don't linger.

nina: i'll sketch the grafana panels and heatmap overlay so maintenance windows show as a hatched region, not just removed. that keeps context.

sre-bot: NOTE: scheduled cordon detected in us-west-2 at 2026-03-16T22:00Z — creating incident annotation id=inc-4921

mira: ok let's aim to get the pushgateway + recording rule in the next sprint. josiah, can you put a PR with the pushgateway hook and a small runbook link?

josiah: yup, will open PR today and ping this thread.

carl: i'll draft the recording rule and run it in staging. quick example for the rule file: 

```
- record: maintenance_window
  expr: max by(node, region) (maintenance_override == 1)
```

then we can update the slo:burn recording to `unless maintenance_window` as above.

mira: thanks all. captures action items. happy to triage if the adjusted EB alerting needs tuning after rollout.

ada: one last thing — we should add a guard to avoid accidental mass-exemptions. e.g., refuse to mark maintenance_override for >10% of fleet without an approver. added that to the playbook.

nina: will make the grafana annotation panel optional per-org so enterprise customers can see raw vs adjusted as they prefer.

sre-bot: ACTION: created task SRE-848 (emit maintenance_override), assigned josiah. ETA 2026-03-22.

mira: great, thanks. :thumbsup:
